channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tengizchevroil's Procurement from Kazakh Suppliers Reaches $53.3 Billion
item.description: Tengizchevroil's (TCO) total procurement of goods and services from Kazakh suppliers has reached $53.3 billion USD. A forum discussed developing Kazakhstan's oil and gas machine-building sector, strengthening industrial potential, and expanding participation of Kazakh enterprises in major oil and gas projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan to change parental leave benefits, fathers to lose eligibility for child-rearing allowance
item.description: Kazakhstan's State Social Insurance Fund announced changes to child-rearing benefits. Starting January 1, 2027, fathers will no longer be eligible for benefits until a child turns 1.5 years old. The fund stated this measure aims to protect mothers and infants, especially during breastfeeding. Fathers will retain the right to parental leave and can receive benefits if they become the sole caregiver.

item.title: Weight and dimension control complexes to be installed at Almaty entrances
item.description: Almaty is installing weight and dimension control systems at its entrances to manage large cargo vehicles. Partial traffic restrictions will be implemented from October 19 to November 19 on the Kuldzha tract and Ili tract. Reversible traffic will be organized on specific 200-meter sections near the city border. The city administration noted that repair timelines may vary due to weather conditions.

item.title: Section of Syganak Street in Almaty temporarily closed for road extension work
item.description: A section of Syganak Street in Almaty will be temporarily closed to traffic from October 17 to October 19 due to road extension work. The closure affects the eastbound lanes from Ryskulov Avenue to Mönke Bi Street, as well as Sharipov Street. Drivers are advised to plan their routes in advance. Over 9,100 video surveillance cameras are being installed in the Almaty region.

item.title: High-speed internet offered in Awaza, Turkmenistan, while connection is slow elsewhere
item.description: High-speed 5G internet services are being offered in Awaza, Turkmenistan, exclusively for visitors. Access is restricted to the tourist zone, with connections immediately cut off outside. Local residents report that obtaining the service requires proof of hotel stay and is calculated based on the number of days spent in Awaza.

item.title: Kazakhstan introduces welfare calculator on eGov for citizens to check and correct their category
item.description: Kazakhstan has launched a welfare calculator on the eGov platform, allowing citizens to check their assigned welfare category (A-E). Vice Minister Bakhtiyar Jazykpaev explained that if data is incorrect or outdated, citizens can submit correction requests through their personal account on eGov or eGov Mobile. The system aims to minimize human error in data.

item.title: Kazakhstan's eGov platform to feature welfare calculator, benefit refusal service, and digital family passports
item.description: Kazakhstan's eGov platform will soon offer a welfare calculator to assess citizens' financial well-being and social stability, considering over 59 indicators. The platform will also introduce a service for refusing benefits and digital family passports. The calculator, developed by the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection, will be available on eGov and eGov Mobile.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce Welfare-Based State Benefits from 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kazakhstan will assign state benefits based on family welfare and need. Approximately 2.2 million middle-class families, with per capita incomes between 203,000-305,000 tenge and owning property, vehicles, or small businesses, may fall into this category. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection stated that these families will not be restricted from 14 types of payments.

item.title: Taliban envoy states Daesh leadership and operational centers fully eliminated in Afghanistan
item.description: The Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan's ambassador to Russia, Gul Hassan Hassan, announced that Daesh leadership and centers have been completely eradicated from Afghan territory. He made these statements during a joint security conference in Moscow attended by the CSTO, CIS, and Shanghai Cooperation Organization.

item.title: Kazakhstan invests 83.4 billion tenge in mechanical engineering projects this year
item.description: Since the beginning of the year, Kazakhstan has invested 83.4 billion tenge into the country's mechanical engineering projects. This significant investment aims to boost development and innovation within the sector.

item.title: Kazakhstan May Temporarily Suspend Benefits for Citizens Refusing Data Verification
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection stated that social payments may be temporarily suspended for citizens who refuse to consent to the processing of their personal data for the 'Digital Family Map' initiative. Vice Minister Bakhytzhan Zhazypbayev explained that integration with second-tier banks is planned to assess family welfare.

item.title: Kenes Rakishev Aims to Utilize Own Gas Processing Plant with Small and Medium Fields
item.description: Fincraft Group plans to increase the utilization of its Borankol Gas Processing Plant in western Kazakhstan to 1.2 billion cubic meters annually within two to three years. Majority shareholder Kenes Rakishev stated the plant will process gas from small and medium-sized fields. This volume represents about a third of the plant's total capacity.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Service for Voluntary Refusal of State Benefits
item.description: Over 200 citizens in Kazakhstan have voluntarily opted out of state benefits after receiving SMS notifications. The Ministry of Labor has launched a new online service via the eGov Mobile app, allowing affluent citizens to decline social payments without visiting government offices. This initiative aims to optimize social assistance measures and ensure transparent fund allocation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Explains Rationale Behind Categorizing Citizens by Welfare (C, D, E)
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection is introducing a welfare categorization system (A-E) for citizens, effective January 1, 2027. Categories C, D, and E will determine the level of state support, with increased assistance for more vulnerable families. The focus for categories D and E will be on employment support and skills training.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses Progress of Artificial Intelligence Projects and Integration Plans
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing the widespread use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. A dialogue was held on the current state of AI projects, focusing on integration into public administration, healthcare, transport, energy, and agriculture. The country has established legal frameworks and a national AI development strategy until 2030.

item.title: Tashkent plans construction of BRT lines on four more road sections
item.description: Tashkent plans to build dedicated bus rapid transit (BRT) lanes along 17.9 kilometers across four new road sections. This initiative aims to improve public transport speed and convenience, making it a more attractive alternative to private cars and reducing city's reliance on them.

item.title: Kazakhstan tax authorities report nearly 30 billion tenge in additional customs duties
item.description: Kazakhstan's State Revenue Committee reported collecting 19.6 billion tenge and assessing an additional 29.6 billion tenge in customs duties during January-September 2026. Violations were found in 84% of customs inspections, with issues including incorrect customs valuation and goods classification.

item.title: Almaty completes urban improvement works on several city street sections
item.description: Almaty is finalizing urban improvement projects on several city streets, covering approximately 34 kilometers. The works focus on creating a comfortable, safe, and modern urban environment, including updated pedestrian and cycling infrastructure, new sidewalks, and green space development.

item.title: 9,100 Surveillance Cameras to Be Installed in Almaty Region for Public Safety and Traffic Control
item.description: A unified video surveillance system, comprising 9,100 cameras, will be implemented in the Almaty region to monitor public safety and traffic order. The project, under a public-private partnership, includes 6,800 fixed cameras and 2,300 pan-tilt cameras. The system aims to prevent offenses, aid in crime resolution, and ensure security.

item.title: Kazakhstan to End Paternity Leave Payments for Childcare After 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, fathers in Kazakhstan will no longer receive childcare benefits for children up to 1.5 years old; these payments will be exclusively for mothers. The State Social Insurance Fund stated this measure aims to protect maternity and childhood. Fathers can still take parental leave, and if the mother works, the family will continue to receive the benefit.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Labor Ministry: Paternity Leave Payments to Cease
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection announced a significant change in childcare benefit allocation. Minister Askarbek Ertayev stated that starting from 2027, only mothers will receive "maternity" benefits, aimed at supporting maternal and child health. Fathers can still take parental leave, but will not receive the payment, which will go to the mother.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Explains Eligibility for Social Benefits Based on Family Income Categories
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection outlined new criteria for social benefits, effective 2027, based on family income categories. Minister Askarbek Ertayev explained that 14 types of benefits will be preserved for families in categories C, D, and E (low to average income), while categories A and B will not receive these payments. Category C includes families with average monthly income between 203,000 and 305,000 tenge per person.

item.title: Large Hashish Shipment Seized in Tyumen with KNB Involvement
item.description: A significant quantity of hashish has been seized in Tyumen. The National Security Committee (KNB) was involved in the operation that led to the confiscation of the illicit drug shipment.

item.title: US Dollar Trades at 452.5 Tenge on Kazakhstan Stock Exchange
item.description: The average weighted exchange rate of the US dollar on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange decreased by 1.40 tenge on Friday, reaching 452.51 tenge. The national currency strengthened against the dollar.

item.title: Climate change may force 40 million South Asians to migrate, UN reports
item.description: Climate change impacts like rising sea levels, floods, and droughts pose serious threats to livelihoods in South Asia, potentially forcing 40 million people to migrate. The UN's International Organization for Migration suggests modern technologies and timely measures can reduce damages.

item.title: Ancient Human Migrations Possibly Linked to Soi Havzak Site in Tajikistan
item.description: Archaeological research at the Soi Havzak Paleolithic site in Tajikistan, discovered in 2023, has concluded. Jointly conducted by Tajik and Israeli institutions with international participation, the findings suggest a link to ancient human migrations. The site, dated between 40,000 and 130,000 years old, yielded stone artifacts and animal bone fragments.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Build Second and Third Nuclear Power Plants, President Mirziyoyev Confirms
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to construct a second and third nuclear power plant, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced during an open dialogue with investors in the fuel and energy sector. The country is increasing uranium production and has gained significant experience, justifying the focus on nuclear energy development. The first plant is under construction in Jizzakh region.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Chair International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea for 2027-2029
item.description: Uzbekistan has been elected to chair the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (IFAS) for the 2027-2029 term. Priorities include improving the fund's framework, water-energy-environment agenda, involving Afghanistan, and promoting water conservation. Uzbekistan proposed 2026-2036 as a decade of action for rational water use in Central Asia.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Criminal Liability for Violating Presidential Administration Immunity
item.description: Uzbekistan has enacted a law establishing criminal responsibility for violating the inviolability and immunity of presidential administration officials and other state body representatives. The law, effective October 15, imposes penalties including imprisonment for up to five years for such offenses.

item.title: Regional Partners Discuss Trans-Afghan Corridor and CASA Railway Progress in Astana
item.description: Officials from Kazakhstan, Afghanistan, Uzbekistan, Pakistan, and Iran met in Astana to advance the Trans-Afghan transport corridor and the Central Asia-South Asia (CASA) railway project. Discussions focused on improving regional connectivity, expanding trade routes, route coordination, infrastructure development, financing, and attracting investors. The CASA railway aims to enhance transport links between Central, South, and West Asia.

item.title: IMF Head Warns of Declining Global Economic Resilience Amid Multiple Shocks
item.description: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva stated the global economy's resilience to shocks is decreasing due to persistent high inflation and dwindling energy and fiscal reserves. Geopolitical conflicts and technological advancements present opposing forces, impacting economic growth differently across nations. The IMF urges action to support vulnerable economies.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes Investor Council for Fuel and Energy Sector
item.description: Uzbekistan will establish an Investor Council for the Fuel and Energy Sector, led by Saida Mirziyoyeva, to streamline investment processes. The council aims to quickly resolve issues faced by investors from land allocation to project launch, reducing bureaucracy and corruption, according to President Mirziyoyev.

item.title: Former US diplomat suggests Afghan unity and international pressure could aid Taliban negotiations
item.description: A former senior US diplomat, Annie Pforzheimer, believes that greater unity among Afghans around common principles, combined with international pressure, could eventually help bring Taliban authorities to the negotiating table. She stated that the Taliban are not currently ready for meaningful political negotiations, but circumstances could change if Afghans present a more unified position.

item.title: CSTO Chief: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan is a long-term political actor, member states increase engagement
item.description: The Secretary-General of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO), Talatbek Masadykov, stated that the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (IEA) has become a long-term political actor. He noted that most CSTO member states are intensifying bilateral engagement with IEA officials to promote economic development, social stability, and reduce security risks originating from Afghanistan.

item.title: Witness in Sanjar Bokayev Case Detained Outside Almaty Court
item.description: A witness in the case of civil activist Sanjar Bokayev was detained outside the Almalinsky District Court in Almaty on October 16. Videos show six police officers and several plainclothes individuals detaining the man. Bokayev's lawyers stated the detained individual was Akhlyddin Khamrakulov, a key witness, and requested the video evidence be added to the case file.

item.title: Uzbekistan to End State Monopoly on Liquefied Gas Supply
item.description: Uzbekistan will abolish the state monopoly on the supply of liquefied gas, impacting 3.8 million households currently using it. President emphasized ensuring uninterrupted supply, safety, and quality of service during this transition. The move aims to liberalize the sector and improve service delivery to consumers.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Develop National Master Plan for Energy Sector Until 2050
item.description: Uzbekistan will develop and publicly release its first National Master Plan for the energy sector, projecting to 2050. The plan will detail regional electricity demand growth, infrastructure needs, and optimal locations for new power generation. This initiative aims to guide long-term investor planning and integrate "green" energy sources.

item.title: International Business and Investment Forum G10 Held in Dushanbe
item.description: Dushanbe hosted the G10 international forum focused on business and investment, organized as part of the 'Tajikistan, Forward!' initiative. Participants discussed entrepreneurship development, foreign capital attraction, digital commerce, and transitioning business ideas into successful projects, according to NIAT 'Khovar'.

item.title: Banks and Digital Platforms Enhance Fraud Protection Measures
item.description: Financial fraud in Uzbekistan has significantly increased, with cybercrimes rising from 863 in 2019 to 58,800 in 2024. The Interior Ministry reports that 98% of cybercrimes in 2024 involved bank cards, often through social engineering rather than technical breaches, highlighting the need for user awareness.

item.title: Private Sector to be Involved in Electricity Distribution Networks in Jizzakh and Tashkent Regions
item.description: A pilot project initiated in the Samarkand region is planned to be implemented in two more regions, Jizzakh and Tashkent. This initiative aims to involve the private sector in electricity distribution networks. Tax incentives for energy-saving projects will also be clarified.
